Design.evidence_source: In this paper, we provide the first direct empirical test of the popular hypothesis that individuals avoid information because of image concerns. We do this by comparing rates of information avoidance in the classic setting—built off of Dana, Weber and Kuang (2007)—to a new setting that only differs by removing selfish motives and thus, as detailed below, removes image concerns to avoid information.
